items.quote: for on the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I hallowed unto me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast: mine shall they be: I am the LORD.
items.claim: The text says the LORD made all of Israel's firstborn, both human and animal, holy to himself on the day he struck down the firstborn of Egypt, and says they belong to him.
items.object: all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast
items.mechanism: a claim of divine ownership tied to the killing of Egypt's firstborn

items.quote: And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine;
items.claim: The text says the LORD took the Levites from among the Israelites in place of all the firstborn, so the Levites belong to him.
items.action: took the Levites as a substitute
items.object: the Levites, in place of all the firstborn of the children of Israel
items.mechanism: a substitution: the Levites are given to the LORD in place of the firstborn, who already belong to him

items.quote: 3:13 Because all the firstborn are mine;
items.claim: The text gives the LORD's ownership of all firstborn as the reason the Levites are taken in their place.
items.mechanism: the reason given for taking the Levites

items.quote: 3:11 And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
items.claim: The text presents these statements as words the LORD spoke to Moses. (Identifying this passage as Numbers 3:11-13 is a model-prior and is not stated in the document.)
items.mechanism: framed as a direct divine speech
